_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**`--format toon` on `rag query` silently degrades to text output.**

`RagAction::Query::format` is typed as the full `WireFormat` (Text/Json/Toon), but the dispatch only distinguishes Json vs. everything-else (`matches!(format, WireFormat::Json)`), so `Toon` is accepted by clap yet silently rendered as plain text. Every other command in this file handles all three `WireFormat` variants explicitly. Either restrict `--format` here to a smaller Text/Json enum, or wire `rag_query_command` to actually support TOON.




<details>
<summary>Proposed fix (restrict to a query-specific format enum)</summary>

```diff
-        /// Output format for results (text or json)
-        #[arg(short, long, default_value = "text")]
-        format: WireFormat,
+        /// Output format for results (text or json)
+        #[arg(short, long, default_value = "text")]
+        format: RagQueryFormat,
```
And reject/handle `Toon` explicitly in `rag_query_command`, or map it to an error rather than silently falling back to text.
</details>


Also applies to: 960-976

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Lost-update race on concurrent indexing of the same matter.**

`index_documents`/`import_legacy` do read-modify-write against the on-disk snapshot (`load_or_empty` → `ingest` → `save`) with no locking. Two concurrent processes indexing the same `matter_id` will both load the pre-existing snapshot, and the later `save` silently overwrites the other's additions. The shared, non-unique `rag.snapshot.tmp` filename in `save` (Line 65) makes this worse: concurrent writers can clobber each other's staged temp file before either rename executes.

Given the CLI can be invoked repeatedly (and this same engine backs the MCP query path per `crates/xberg/src/mcp/rag.rs`), this is worth guarding — e.g. a per-matter file lock (`fs2`/`fslock`) around the read-modify-write, or at minimum a unique tmp filename (PID/UUID suffix) to avoid the staging-file collision.





Also applies to: 136-175
